canonical.title: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick
canonical.sourceFilePath: 14. Dynamic Programming/8. DP on Partition/02. Minimum cost to cut stick.cpp

narrative.title: The Marble Slab Cutting Bay
narrative.scenario: A stone workshop must slice a marble slab at a list of marked positions. Each pass of the saw bills the current length of the piece being cut, and the foreman may execute the marks in any order. Scheduling smartly — cutting expensive pieces apart early — can slash the invoice, so the shop wants the cheapest total billing plan.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n (stick length) and an array cuts of distinct cut positions.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the minimum total cost to perform all cuts, where each cut costs the length of the piece cut.

testCases.explanation: Cutting 1, then 5, then 3, then 4 keeps every billed length small — total 16.
Order 2, 1, 4, 5, 6 achieves the minimum billing of 22.

hintLevels: Level 1: Sort the cut positions and pad the ends with 0 and n so every piece has computable boundaries.
Level 2: For the span between boundary i and j, try each interior cut k last: cost = span length + both halves.
Level 3: Choosing the LAST cut (not the first) is what makes the two subproblems independent.
